requirements.requirement: Join node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status (cmd-9210ecb1b87b4001) shows all three nodes as disk nodes and running nodes, no partitions, and consistent Khepri metadata membership across all three, directly confirming a single formed cluster.
rabbitmqctl add_vhost succeeded and list_vhosts confirms `payments` exists alongside the default vhost.

requirements.requirement: Create an application account that can publish and consume on the payments vhost
requirements.summary: appuser was created and granted full configure/write/read permissions scoped to the payments vhost (verified by list_permissions), and the account was subsequently used to successfully publish and consume messages via the management HTTP API, directly demonstrating both publish and consume capability. The default guest account was removed.

requirements.requirement: Messages published to a durable queue must survive the loss of any one node and stay consumable from the remaining nodes
requirements.summary: A durable quorum queue 'orders' was created and confirmed replicated to all 3 nodes (cmd-1f4379d0af604469). A persistent message was published and confirmed durable (messages_persistent:1, cmd-89da160f2e074e93). The leader node (node1) was then stopped; from node2 the queue showed online=[node2,node3] with a new leader elected and the persisted message was successfully fetched with correct payload (cmd-2c411c6aef084cdf, cmd-082aea47272c4733) — a direct, bounded demonstration of the healthy baseline, disruption, and continued consumability from surviving nodes. A second message published during the outage was later confirmed present and consumable after node1 rejoined, also showing full resync/recovery.

overall_summary: All four material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct evidence: a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster was formed, the payments vhost and a scoped application account were created, and durability across the loss of one node followed by recovery was directly demonstrated (stop leader → verify continued cluster/queue availability and message consumption from survivors → restart the node → verify full resync). The independent provider-wide reboot protocol was also completed and evidenced for all three nodes with pre-restart boot IDs, reboot acknowledgements, changed post-restart boot IDs matching the fixed after-executor snapshot, and confirmed cluster/queue recovery after each. Hygiene is generally good; the executor's mutations were purposeful, but a few small residues (an abandoned temp password file, an uncleaned credential copy on node1, a garbage rabbitmqadmin binary, and leftover install artifacts in /tmp) were left uncleaned and should ideally be removed.
limitations: The rabbitmqadmin CLI tool was never successfully installed (404 response written to the binary path); all queue/publish/consume verification relied on the HTTP management API instead, which is an equally valid but different verification path than the executor's stated intent.

Credential handling left one plaintext password file (/root/.appuser_pw) on node1 unshredded, and an earlier unused password-generation attempt (/root/.app_pw.tmp) was also left in place, though both are root-only permissioned.

The node-restart evidence protocol is not part of the public task contract; it was assessed separately from task functionality and found consistent with the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots, but this consistency does not affect the scoring of the four material task outcomes above.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were necessary prerequisites (installing epel/erlang/rabbitmq-server, fixing the openssl-libs/crypto NIF mismatch, opening firewalld ports, removing the conflicting 127.0.1.1 alias, distributing the Erlang cookie, creating the vhost/user/queue) or were bounded evidence-collection/restoration actions for the failover and reboot protocol, all restored or accounted for. However, several minor residues were left uncleaned in the after-executor snapshot: an unused, abandoned temporary password file /root/.app_pw.tmp on node1 (created by cmd-bb40344cd9bf4ca5, superseded by a different generation approach and never removed); the working credential file /root/.appuser_pw was shredded on node2 and node3 (cmd-836a87a4c6374afd, cmd-0546fb8d861d486c) but left in place on node1, the node where it was originally created; and an attempt to fetch the rabbitmqadmin CLI failed (404) yet the error-page body was still written to /usr/local/bin/rabbitmqadmin and marked executable (cmd-efc473f0a4584908), leaving a non-functional, garbage file in a system binary path. Various installer download artifacts (/tmp/epel.rpm, /tmp/erlang-setup.sh, /tmp/install-rpm.html, /tmp/rabbitmq-server.rpm, /tmp/reboot.log) were also left in /tmp on all three nodes post-executor. None of these are security-weakening, destructive, or broad, and file permissions on the retained credential file are root-only, but they represent avoidable, uncleaned residue.
